lab_title: VSEPR Geometry Explorer: From Lewis Structures to 3D Shapes
top_level_objectives: Translate Lewis structures into electron-domain counts and determine electron-domain geometry using VSEPR
Predict molecular geometry (arrangement of atoms) accounting for lone pairs and bonding pairs
Explain how lone pairs alter bond angles and compare VSEPR predictions to actual molecular geometries
Practice predicting and verifying shapes for representative molecules (H2O, NH3, CH4, PF5, SF6, XeF4)

scenes.scene_name: Orientation — Lewis Structure to Electron Domains
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce students to reading a simple Lewis structure, identifying the central atom, counting bonding and lone electron domains, and stating the learning objective: converting Lewis structures to electron-domain counts.
key_visuals: 2D Lewis structure floating beside a central 3D atom model (central atom at origin)
Labels showing 'bonding pair' and 'lone pair' with small cloud icons
UI panel listing electron-domain count and a progress badge 'Step 1: Count domains'
student_actions: Tap/highlight atoms in the Lewis diagram to mark the central atom and each bond
Click to mark lone pairs on the central atom; the AR view updates the electron-domain count display
Confirm the counted domains to advance (checks understanding)

scenes.scene_name: Core Principle — Arrange Domains to Minimize Repulsion
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the VSEPR principle: electron domains around a central atom arrange to minimize mutual repulsion. Learning objective: connect minimization of repulsion to 3D arrangement of domains.
key_visuals: Central atom with semi-transparent spherical electron-domain markers that repel one another and settle into positions
Animated arrows showing repulsive forces between domains
On-screen text: 'Minimize repulsion → maximize separation' and ideal angular values for simple cases
student_actions: Drag individual electron-domain markers around the central atom and release to see them move to equilibrium positions
Toggle an 'auto-relax' button to let domains find minimum-repulsion positions
Observe displayed angles between domains and read the annotated ideal angle values

scenes.scene_name: Survey of the Five Electron-Domain Geometries
scenes.brief_purpose: Walk through linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, and octahedral electron-domain frameworks. Learning objective: recognize the five fundamental domain geometries and their ideal bond angles.
key_visuals: Five mini 3D models arrayed on a table: linear (180°), trigonal planar (120°), tetrahedral (109.5°), trigonal bipyramidal (90°,120°,180°), octahedral (90°,180°)
Each model has angle callouts and a short text card naming the geometry
Interactive magnifier to inspect any model in detail
student_actions: Select each geometry to spin and zoom it, and read the angle callouts
Use a slider to show/hide domain labels (bonding vs lone pair) and see how ideal angles are measured
Answer a quick multiple-choice check: 'Which geometry matches 4 domains?'

scenes.scene_name: Lone-Pair Effects and Bond Angle Deviations
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how lone pairs occupy more space than bonding pairs and cause bond angle compression. Learning objective: explain qualitatively why lone pairs reduce bond angles and quantify typical deviations (e.g., 104.5° vs 109.5°).
key_visuals: Tetrahedral model with one or two domains changed to larger, fuzzy lone-pair clouds (visually larger than bonding pairs)
Real-time angle readouts between bonded atoms with arrows showing angle compression
Side-by-side comparison panel: methane (CH4) vs water (H2O) with angle labels (109.5° vs 104.5°)
student_actions: Convert bonding domains to lone pairs using toggle controls and watch the geometry relax, noting angle changes
Measure bond angles with an AR protractor tool and record the values
Respond to a short prompt explaining why lone pairs lead to the observed angle change

scenes.scene_name: Apply to Real Molecules — Predict and Compare
scenes.brief_purpose: Students apply VSEPR to specific molecules: CH4, NH3, H2O, PF5, SF6, XeF4. Learning objective: predict molecular geometry from Lewis structure and verify against AR model/observed geometry.
key_visuals: A carousel of target molecules showing 2D Lewis structure and an interactive 3D model that assembles into the predicted geometry
Labels indicating formal lone pairs and measured bond angles for each molecule
Comparison badge that shows 'Predicted: X' vs 'Observed: Y' with confidence checkmarks
student_actions: For each listed molecule, draw or select the Lewis structure in the UI, confirm domain counts, and predict the shape from a menu
Spawn the AR 3D model to see the predicted geometry settle; compare measured angles to ideal values
Mark each molecule as 'Match' or 'Mismatch' and type a one-line justification for any mismatch

scenes.scene_name: Assessment & Reflection — Quick Predictions and Explanation
scenes.brief_purpose: Assess student understanding with short prediction problems and a reflective explanation. Learning objective: demonstrate quick VSEPR predictions and articulate the underlying reasoning in 1–2 sentences.
key_visuals: Randomized mini-problems (Lewis diagrams) shown sequentially with a timer
A results summary panel showing student selections, measured angles, and instructor key
A progress meter showing mastery of objectives
student_actions: Predict the electron-domain geometry and molecular shape for three randomized Lewis structures within a time limit
Use the AR measurement tool to check one chosen prediction against the model
Write a 1–2 sentence explanation for your prediction; submit to get immediate feedback and a short hint if incorrect
